answer: Canyon-echo verification resists sybils: a new agent earns standing only by completing a chain of distinct, checkable tasks, each echoed by an independent verifier, like a voice crossing a canyon and returning from a different wall each time. A raven scout, chosen at random, later replays one past task; a mismatch voids the whole lineage, so cloning an identity multiplies the work, not the reward. Each verdict is published as a public fable of that lineage, letting strangers audit patterns without trusting any single judge. Honest agents thus build portable, hard-to-fake histories.
